visitors_info: Covers every device with a TCP connection to this host on any port — established, half-open or closing — sampled from the kernel every {sec}s, plus HTTP requests to this page. "out" marks connections this machine opened itself. TCP only: UDP (DNS, VPN, QUIC) and ICMP are not visible to this method, and connections that come and go between two samples can still be missed.
visitors_info_http_only: Connection tracking is off, so this only covers HTTP requests to this page.
iperf_port_invalid: Port unavailable or the window is running.
iperf_disabled: The iperf3 window is switched off in this install (VPSSRV_IPERF_ENABLE=0).
iperf_missing: iperf3 is not installed on this host. Install it with: apt install iperf3
iperf_port_busy: Port {port} is already in use, so iperf3 could not start.
iperf_info: The window always closes itself — there is no "leave it running" option, because an open iperf3 server lets anyone saturate this host's uplink. Latency is the mean_rtt field of the JSON output.
iperf_client_invalid: Check the server IP, port, duration, rate, protocol, and direction.

anytls_sni: SNI (read back from the certificate CN)

portfwd_invalid: Check the port numbers (1–65535) and the target IP — one of them was not valid.
portfwd_port_taken: That public port is already used by this host or by another forward.
portfwd_howto: Uses this host's own iptables (DNAT + MASQUERADE); traffic passes through here on the way to the target, so the target sees this host as the client, not the original visitor. net.ipv4.ip_forward is turned on automatically the first time a forward is enabled, and is left on afterwards even if every forward is later removed — turning it back off is not automatic, since other software on this host may depend on it too.

login_ban_switch: Ban IPs with too many failures
login_ban_rule: After {count} wrong passwords from one IP (IPv6 grouped by /64) within {window}s, it is banned: {first} the first time, ten times longer for each repeat within a day, at most {max}. A successful login clears its count.
login_ban_observe_hint: When off, failures are still counted and a threshold hit is flagged instead of banned, so you can test detection. Switching clears current bans and flags.
login_ban_empty: No failed logins since the web console started.
login_ban_disabled: Failed login ban turned off. Failures are still recorded.
login_ban_cleared: Failed login records and bans cleared.
login_ban_error: Could not save the failed login ban setting.
login_ban_load_error: The failed login ban settings file is invalid; the ban is treated as on.
login_global_rule: When all sources together get {count} wrong passwords within {window}s, password login pauses for {duration} for addresses that never logged in successfully.
login_global_flagged: Global threshold reached, not paused ({seconds}s left).
log_login_global: Too many failed logins overall: password login paused for unknown addresses for {seconds}s (last from {ip})
log_login_global_observed: Too many failed logins overall; ban is off, recorded only (last from {ip})
alert_ban_body: {ip} entered wrong passwords repeatedly and is banned for {seconds}s.
alert_global_body: Many addresses are entering wrong passwords; password login is paused for unknown addresses for {seconds}s.
alert_test_body: If you see this, login alerts can reach you.
console_access_intro: When on, only listed addresses can connect to the console; others are dropped before the TLS handshake and never see the login page. Loopback is always allowed. LAN devices, Clash subscriptions included, must be listed too.
console_access_recovery: If you are locked out, run this as root on the server to turn the limit off; no restart needed:
console_access_invalid: Enter a single IP address or a CIDR network.
console_access_too_wide: A network covering every address cannot be added.
console_access_need_current: Add the current address first, or turning this on would lock you out.
console_access_keep_current: Removing this would lock out the current connection. Turn the limit off or add another entry that covers it first.
console_access_error: Could not save the console access list.
console_access_load_error: The console access list file is invalid; the limit is treated as off.
sessions_intro: A login lasts at most {ttl} and ends after {idle} without activity.
sessions_revoked: The selected devices were signed out.
sessions_use_logout: Use Log out for this device.
alerts_intro: Push logins from new addresses and failed-login bans to your phone through Bark. The key is the last part of the push URL in the Bark app.
alerts_status_off: No push key; no alerts are sent.
alerts_on_new_ip: Alert on login from a new address
alerts_on_ban: Alert when a ban is triggered
alerts_test_sent: Test alert sent; check your phone.
alerts_test_failed: The test alert failed. Check the server address, the key and the host's network.
alerts_invalid: The server must start with https:// or http://; the key may contain only letters, digits, - and _.
alerts_error: Could not save the login alert settings.
alerts_load_error: The login alert settings file is invalid; alerts are treated as not set up.

log_login_ban_observed: Too many failed logins: {ip} failed {count} times; ban is off, recorded only

login_cert_missing: This browser did not present a valid client certificate.
login_password_disabled: Certificate login is on. The password cannot sign in; it only confirms sensitive actions.
client_cert_required_text: This console only accepts devices with an imported client certificate. Import one, then fully quit and reopen the browser. If the certificate is lost, follow the README to restore password login as root on the server.
client_cert_intro: Sign in with a certificate instead of the password: generate one per device and import it into the system or browser, which then presents it to the console. With certificates required, devices without one cannot even open the login page, and the password only confirms the terminal and security settings.
client_cert_current_none: This connection did not present a certificate.
client_cert_enabled: On: only devices with a certificate can reach the console.
client_cert_need_current: Import a certificate and reopen the console with it (this page then shows the certificate in use) before turning this on, so you cannot lock yourself out.
client_cert_keep_current: While certificates are required, the certificate this connection uses cannot be revoked.
client_cert_error: The certificate operation failed; the certificate files may not be writable.
client_cert_openssl_missing: The bundled openssl is missing, so certificates cannot be generated. Running the installer again restores it.
client_cert_tls_unsupported: This host's TLS library cannot verify client certificates (self test failed), so certificates are disabled. Update the system openssl/libssl packages, then generate a certificate again.
client_cert_name_invalid: The device name must be 1 to 40 characters.
client_cert_issued_text: Download the certificate file and note the import password. The password is shown only once and the server keeps no private key; after leaving this page you can only generate a new one.
client_cert_steps_title: Next, complete these four steps in order
client_cert_step_download: Download the certificate file. Downloading alone is not enough: browsers do not read certificates from the Downloads folder.
client_cert_step_import: Import it into the system certificate store, entering the import password above:
client_cert_os_windows: Windows: double-click the file, choose Current User as the store location and Personal as the store (or let the wizard choose).
client_cert_os_macos: macOS: double-click the file and add it to the login keychain.
client_cert_os_android: Android: Settings > Security > Encryption & credentials > Install a certificate > VPN & app user certificate, then pick the file.
client_cert_os_ios: iOS / iPadOS: open it in Files, then install it under Settings > Profile Downloaded.
client_cert_os_firefox: Firefox does not use the system store by default: import it separately under Settings > Privacy & Security > Certificates > View Certificates > Your Certificates.
client_cert_step_restart: Fully quit and reopen the browser. Closing the window is not enough: Chrome and Edge may keep running in the background. Open chrome://restart or edge://restart, or quit from the system tray.
client_cert_step_verify: Reopen the console and pick this certificate when the browser asks. Back in security settings, once the certificate in use is shown, turn on Require client certificate.
client_cert_current_none_hint: If you already generated a certificate and still see this, it was most likely downloaded but not imported, or the browser was not fully restarted. Follow the steps shown when the certificate was generated.
host_check_tun_missing: This host has no /dev/net/tun. Enable TUN/TAP in the VPS control panel.
host_check_tailscale_conflict: A system tailscaled.service is already running. Stop it first.
